hero.caption: After the Battle of Cover Mountain in the American Civil War, Union General William W. Averell led his force to the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad. After destroying a small segment of the rail line, he began a difficult route north in rain and mountainous terrain while pursued by Confederate forces.
hero.alt: After the Battle of Cover Mountain in the American Civil War, Union General William W. Averell led his force to the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad. images.caption: During May 1864 in the American Civil War, Union General William W. Averell tried to lure his pursuer into mountainous terrain where Averell would have an advantage. Averell's target was Wytheville, Virginia and nearby lead mines. Confederate General John H. Morgan was not fooled and took the shortest route to Wytheville, and his forces stopped Averell north of Wytheville at a mountain pass.

images.caption: This shows the approximate positions of troops at the Battle of Cove Mountain in the American Civil War, although they moved around--especially the 34th OVMI. Positioning is based on a New York Times article from May 22, 1864; the book History of the Second Regiment, West Virginia Cavalry Volunteers; Averell's OR, and the book 13th Kentucky Cavalry, CSA: "Caudill's Army".
